text: The Patriots bid farewell to one of their greatest defenders this week as Stephon Gilmore, the 2019 NFL Defensive Player of the Year and two-time All-Pro, signed a one-day contract Friday to retire as a member of New England, cementing his legacy as one of the franchise's most dominant cornerbacks in history. On the injury front, running back TreVeyon Henderson expressed confidence he's "ready to go" for Sunday's home opener against the Steelers after missing Week 1 with an ankle injury, though the team will have to monitor starting cornerback Carlton Davis III, who remains questionable heading into the matchup. Meanwhile, the Patriots organization continues its promotional blitz for the upcoming Munich game with an unusual spectacle: Hall of Famer Adam Vinatieri will attempt a Guinness World Record field goal kick at Jungfraujoch in the Swiss Alps, and owner Robert Kraft made headlines by having Macklemore removed as an opening act for Ed Sheeran's Gillette Stadium shows due to what Kraft described as a "history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery" offensive to the Jewish community.
